github-compat.summary: Most of the round-1 github-compat findings are genuinely fixed, verified against the current tree, not the claims. Major #1 (material-change never skips): FIXED — material-change.mjs now compares a whitelist of owner-driven fields (login, name, memberSince, publicRepos, totalCommits, totalSourceBytes, languages, lastPush, recentPushes, featured); I simulated a quiet week (capturedAt, window boundaries, sliding weekly buckets, methods.activity all advanced) and it compares equal, so exit 3 skips the commit; the contributions-only staleness trade-off is documented in the script header and docs/maintenance.md. Major #3 (no README drift gate): FIXED — ci.yml regenerates README.md and docs/tokens.md and fails on git diff. Major #4: two of three parts FIXED — both workflows pin actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5... and actions/setup-node@8207627860... which I verified via the GitHub API resolve to the claimed v7.0.1/v7.0.0 tags, and both declare concurrency groups — but the commit message part is unresolved (see unresolved). Overflow #1 (topics/descriptions): RESOLVED — gh api shows all four featured repos with English descriptions and non-empty topics matching .ai/reports/cross-repo.md and the committed snapshot; T-008 is CLAUDE_TESTED with topics ledgered, and T-012 remaining PLANNED honestly reflects that final acceptance awaits this review. Overflow #2 (Active work): RESOLVED — the section exists with two bullets from snapshotted recentPushes plus the private-work sentence, exactly per brief §8.7; the README's 8 picture blocks match the brief's own 8 image slots (BACKLOG AC3's 'nine' contradicts the brief, not the implementation). All six minors resolved or substantially resolved: distinct exit codes 0/3/1 with the workflow failing on unexpected codes; GitHub/LinkedIn casing and channel order correct; stale references to qa:platform/motion.test.ts/variants.test.ts gone; SIZE_LIMITS now the brief's 90/45/400 KB (payload measures 333 KB); package.json says 'HDU // Engineering Record'; the 60-day auto-disable is documented and a real link check (with a Medium RSS workaround per brief §8.9) lives in qa:github. Gates all pass from the repo root: tsc clean, 62/62 tests, validate 0 errors, render --check 18/18; animation remains confined to the hero pair (the motion-system plate grep hit is the word 'animations' in its accessible desc); reduced-motion picture-source ordering intact; sanitizer-safe HTML only. However, two confirmed-major residues are neither fixed nor ledgered, so the verdict is FAIL on those alone: (1) the T-010 binding '>50% decrease' guard was replaced by an absolute sanity floor that never inspects contributions/activity values — my simulation shows a zeroed-but-structurally-complete contribution calendar coinciding with any owner push (guaranteed eventually under a persistent token failure, the exact failure T-010 names as most likely) passes the floor, registers as material, self-consistently validates, and is committed unattended, while the workflow comment claims 'a degraded API response fails the job here'; (2) the refresh commit message is still 'chore(telemetry): refresh measured data' with no measurement date and no [skip ci] — the third clause of confirmed major #4, absent from STATUS.md's 16 deviations and silently dropped from round-1.md's own resolution ledger. Both are cheap to fix (one contributions>0-plus-decrease check or a ledger entry; one commit-message template). Residual minor notes, none blocking: no SHA-review-cadence or graph-inflation disclosure in docs (the latter largely moot since commits are now conditional and bot-authored); the description-less Active-work bullet renders as '— last push 2026-08.' (lowercase, degenerate); recentPushes descriptions are interpolated into Markdown unescaped (owner-controlled, low risk); cross-repo.md's correction block still quotes the superseded 'for a storefront' live description one revision behind the actual one. No new critical/major regressions found in the fix-wave diff within this lens.

security-hygiene.summary: All round-1 security-hygiene findings are genuinely resolved in the current tree. The single confirmed major (audit-mandated font-licence validator gate absent) is implemented at scripts/validate/validate-all.ts:130-149 — it errors on font binaries without a licence file AND on a missing PROVENANCE.md, and I proved it empirically in a scratchpad copy: removing LICENSE-JetBrainsMono.txt makes npm run validate print ERROR [font-licence] and exit 1; the gate runs in both CI and the refresh workflow's pre-commit verify step, and the vendored fonts are untouched since the originally sha-verified commit. All three minors are resolved: (1) both workflows now pin actions to full commit SHAs which I independently resolved against the live GitHub API and confirmed match the claimed tags (checkout v7.0.1, setup-node v7.0.0), with concurrency groups added; (2) the 60-day scheduled-workflow auto-disable is documented in docs/maintenance.md with the re-enable path; (3) the public .ai/ exposure is explicitly accepted as STATUS.md deviation 14. Regression sweep found no new critical/major issues: secrets grep over all 128 tracked files and post-round-1 history is clean (no tokens, keys, or local user paths; only the sanctioned public contact email); the new recentPushes/Active-work pipeline draws only from a GraphQL query scoped privacy:PUBLIC/isFork:false/OWNER so no private data can leak into the README; material-change.mjs uses execFileSync with array args and distinct exit codes the workflow branches on strictly (crash fails the job); the API token is sent only to api.github.com, never logged, and the qa link-check sends no Authorization header to external hosts; no untrusted input reaches any workflow run block; refresh token stays step-scoped with a correctly read-scoped PROFILE_READ_TOKEN fallback documented; npm audit reports 0 vulnerabilities and typecheck/62 tests/validate/render --check are all green. Non-blocking notes: ci.yml leaves checkout's default persist-credentials with its read-only token; no unit test locks the font-licence gate against a future validator refactor (it is live in both workflows' validate path); deviation 14 slightly overstates the .ai exposure (no user-directory paths actually exist in tracked files).
